name: Mulgara
tagline: Pure-Java RDF triplestore forked from Kowari, with SPARQL and iTQL; dormant since its 2014 release.
description: Mulgara is a transactional RDF triplestore written entirely in Java, forked in 2006 from Tucana's Kowari after Northrop Grumman, which had bought Tucana and owned the Kowari trademark, threatened a developer over new releases. Instead of sitting on a relational database it keeps its own indexes of subject-predicate-object statements, answers SPARQL and the older iTQL language, supports JTA transactions, and integrates with the Jena and Sesame APIs. Development slowed after 2012 and the last release, 2.1.13, was a small auditing fix in February 2014; the code now sits on GitHub with only token activity since. Choose Apache Jena TDB, RDF4J, Oxigraph or a commercial store for anything current.
statusNote: No release since 2.1.13 (Feb 2014); the GitHub repository is dormant. Use Apache Jena TDB, RDF4J or Oxigraph.
strengths: Native triple indexes rather than an RDF layer over SQL
Transactional, with JTA/XA integration for Java applications
Jena and Sesame compatibility eased swapping it into existing code
weaknesses: No releases since 2014 and no active maintainers
SPARQL 1.1 support is incomplete compared with current stores
OSL 3.0 licensing is unusual and less permissive than Apache-licensed peers
useCases: Maintaining legacy semantic-web applications built on it
